merger_description:
AMAL Trustees Limited:

1. acting as trustee for AOP Investment Trust, will acquire an interest of up to a maximum of approximately 12% in the Octopus Australia Sustainable Investments Fund (**OASIS**), and
2. acting as trustee for APG Infra Investments Holding Trust, will increase its interest in OASIS from approximately 27.5% to a maximum of approximately 49%.

Each of the AOP Investment Trust and APG Infra Investments Holding Trust are managed investment trusts, held by AMAL Trustees Ltd. The trusts are both managed by Telopea Real Estate Partners Pty Ltd, an Australian investment manager. The interests in the trusts are both managed by APG Asset Management NV (**APG**), an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP, on behalf of various pension fund clients. APG is a pension fund asset manager based in the Netherlands. APG manages investments for pension fund clients both in the Netherlands and globally.

OASIS is ultimately managed by Octopus Capital Aust Pty Limited (**OCA**). OCA and OASIS, together with their subsidiaries (collectively, **Octopus Australia**), is an Australian-based renewables developer, operator and investment manager. Octopus Australia manages approximately AUD 2 billion in renewable energy assets.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between the acquiring group
(the trusts, APG and Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP) and
Octopus Australia in the supply of electricity generation
services in Australia
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
